study.question: Observation: feature-only, pooled and target-aware reference AUCs are 0.6050036145, 0.6102261137 and 0.6133619861. Aligned full/half AUCs are 0.6149816911798147/0.6151021885074872 and losses 0.19656340759133067/0.19653258393542125. Yet half worsens history_1_16 AUC from0.5768217632267676 to0.5749254769335556 and loss from0.15748992315002142 to0.1579209858133702 (41805 impressions,1444 positives,40361 negatives); empty-history AUC falls from0.5839558467235497 to0.5834990397938595 and loss rises from0.1708970609387225 to0.1719545590021461 (8272,310,7962). Does retaining native normalization derivatives on <=16-event training impressions improve short-history validation ranking and loss while retaining population AUC relative to global half? This is a new exploratory replacement contrast prompted by a previously observed limitation, not a confirmatory subgroup test. The preferred earlier paired-seed closure question remains unanswered: seed43/44 research and checkpoint assessment interfaces are not exposed; final_paired_seeds is not authorization to override seed42. The current runtime instead requires a feasible candidate submission, so submit one bounded mechanism contrast rather than another transport timing sweep or a purported same-seed robustness experiment.
study.hypothesis: Within short nonempty histories, permuting reciprocal-norm backward scales can degrade local relevance learning despite the population benefit of the inherited half rule. A per-impression length-conditioned choice of the full product Jacobian for <=16 supplied events, with half-rank Jacobian allocation retained for longer histories, may recover part of the short-history loss without erasing the population gain. At identical parameters the route changes derivatives only through category/brand product paths; all logits are unchanged. Empty histories have no product-path signal, and eligible singleton histories have identical own/half donors. Any empty-history improvement is indirect shared-parameter adaptation, not direct correction. The observed subgroup pattern alone does not establish this mechanism; generic regularization and global trajectory effects remain plausible.

study.proposed_difference: Add sparse_full_gradient boolean. In grad-enabled normalization, compute the inherited unit and half surrogate; when flag=True use torch.where(mask.sum(-1)<=16, native_unit, half_surrogate). The mask count is causal supplied history, computed independently within each impression; no labels, other users, event additions, sample selection or seed manipulation. Grad-disabled inference remains exactly the inherited native unit shortcut. This route changes where the existing backward rule is applied and adds no parameters. It is mechanism-distinct from global donor allocation, inference shortcuts and identity transport, but remains an inherited-model modification with novelty unverified. Keep only two new modules; reference historical full-gradient and baseline receipts descriptively. Do not claim a length-by-global-gradient factorial, matched optimizer updates, or superiority over historical full from this pair alone.
predictions: At identical raw inputs/parameters, full/global-half/routed normalized products and logits agree within floating-point tolerance. Artificial native full and routed-short VJPs match, as do inherited half and routed-long VJPs; donor identities match an independent Python ranking oracle.

For seed42 the routed candidate should improve history_1_16 AUC and reduce its unweighted Logloss versus the contemporaneous global-half control, without reducing full-population AUC. This is a directional exploratory prediction; the bin was chosen after earlier validation feedback.

Empty-history changes may have either sign because the intervention is indirect there; singleton full/half product derivatives coincide. Zero direct empty-history product-path correction is a structural prediction, not a claim that final empty predictions are invariant.

The flag-off control should reproduce parent population and all inherited slice metrics under the frozen deterministic host recipe. Any discrepancy must be investigated before treating cross-round controls as matched; no claim of bitwise prediction equality follows from matching aggregate metrics.

Parameters should remain17130275; report measured train/wall/peak memory and inference throughput/p50/p95 for both. No efficiency gain is predicted; extra routing may add training cost. Diagnostics are candidate-authored bounded checks, not training-wide certification.
falsifiers: Wrong mask-count boundary at16/17; donor tie/floor/mask errors; nonfinite outputs; changed logits at fixed state; derivative mismatch or unauthorized information/seed/optimizer changes invalidate mechanism attribution. Candidate-authored synthetic VJP scaled errors should be <=1e-5 float32 and <=1e-10 float64; donor errors should be0, forward errors <=1e-6, and synthetic short changed-VJP magnitude should be positive. Validate counts and finite values before interpreting scores.

If short-history AUC fails to increase or its loss fails to decrease, the proposed short-history benefit is unsupported for this implementation. If population AUC falls, the retention prediction fails even if the short bin improves; report the tradeoff without retuning the cutoff or hiding either outcome.

No direct effect on empty histories would refute neither indirect adaptation nor the nonempty routing hypothesis. A claimed direct local empty-history gradient repair would itself contradict the masked model structure.

A null or negative result limits this one routing implementation at seed42; it does not refute every length-dependent optimization mechanism. Positive results do not identify semantic mediation, remove adaptive validation bias or establish multi-seed generalization.
alternative_explanations: Shared embedding/attention adaptation and Adam state change globally; validation short-history regressions may be driven mostly by long-history training, so locally restoring short derivatives may not help.

Generic conditioning/regularization or altered aggregate gradient energy, rather than length-specific relevance failure, can explain an effect. The simple pair estimates the total routing change, not a unique biological/semantic mechanism or a matched-gradient-energy effect.

Fixed seed42, repeated validation and checkpoint selection can create a favorable difference. Independent seeds remain unavailable; even later paired seeds would not remove adaptive validation-selection bias.

Length correlates with user frequency, behavior composition, recency and exposure propensity. Fixed mask-length routing does not identify any one of these as a causal moderator. First512 diagnostic inputs are not a representative sample of the full training or validation population.
Execution state, numerical differences and host timing can confound small cost differences; no efficiency conclusion or same-state optimizer equivalence from a single run pair.

Counts are impression counts with repeated users. Aggregate receipts lack paired prediction vectors/user-cluster IDs, so paired user-cluster confidence intervals, calibration claims, statistical significance and equivalence cannot be computed.
